summary.headline: Metropolis Q4 FY26 organic revenue grew 14.7% to INR 392 crores, with organic EBITDA margin at 27.2%, up from 18.5%.
summary.overview: Organic revenue grew 14.7% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR 392 crores, driven by 9.3% patient volume growth and about 5% realisation improvement, with no price increase taken in the quarter due to GST reasons. Organic EBITDA margin rose to 27.2% (from 18.5%) and full-year organic margin reached 25.9%, up about 140 bps after adjusting for prior-year acquisition costs. Management said the heavy lab and centre build-out is largely done, so the focus shifts to throughput-led productivity, and it guided to 14% to 15% revenue CAGR and a 27% to 28% group EBITDA margin over three years. Core Diagnostics reached a high-single-digit margin in Q4, meeting the 4-quarter turnaround commitment.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY; margin up ~140 bps on normalised basis

financial_highlights.metric: MHL Group EBITDA Q4 FY26 / FY26
financial_highlights.value: Q4: INR 108 crores, margin 25.4%; FY26: INR 401 crores, margin 24.4%

financial_highlights.metric: MHL Group PAT Q4 FY26 / FY26
financial_highlights.value: Q4: INR 51 crores, margin 12%; FY26: INR 191 crores, margin 11.6%

segments.name: B2C (organic)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 14.7% YoY and FY26 grew 14%, supported by wellness, specialty and routine testing across physical and digital channels. Group B2C grew 20% in Q4 and 19% for FY26.

segments.name: B2B (organic)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 14.7% YoY and FY26 grew 13.3%, with focus on ease of doing business and better unit economics. Group B2B grew 28% in Q4 and 31% for FY26.

segments.name: TruHealth
segments.commentary: Organic revenue grew 20% in Q4 and 21% for FY26; contributed 19% of FY26 organic revenue. Group TruHealth contributed 18% and grew 27%.

segments.name: Specialty
segments.commentary: Organic revenue grew 17% in Q4 and 16% for FY26; contributed 37% of FY26 organic revenue. Group Specialty contributed 39% and grew 32%.

segments.name: Core Diagnostics (acquired)
segments.commentary: Margin moved from about negative 2% to high-single-digit in Q4 FY26, completing the 4-quarter commitment. Target is 20%-plus EBITDA margin in 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 14% to 15% over the next 3 years, from volumes, RPP growth and price increases, plus possible acquisitions.
FY27 patient volume growth of 8% to 9%, with the remaining ~5% from realisation.
Group EBITDA margin of 27% to 28% over three years; about 125 to 150 bps improvement expected in the coming year.
Specialty mix expected to reach around 40% this year, per management's response to an analyst.
No price increase planned at present; will consider later in the year if needed.
Lab-to-centre ratio to move from 1:24 toward 1:30 in many markets over 18 months and 1:35 over 3 years; 1,500 more collection centres planned.
100 mini hubs over 3 years (50 upgraded from existing centres, 50 new), each costing about INR 30 to 40 lakh.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR 65 crores; future capex is selective and focused on targeted network additions, specialty tests, technology and digital.
Network added 490 centres in FY26, taking the total to over 5,000 collection centres across more than 750 towns and 212 labs.
Lab addition phase is over; no high number of new labs planned in the coming year.
Genomics: two CAP-accredited genomic labs (Gurgaon and Mumbai); barcoding rolled out across 220 labs.
Centre productivity target: +20% over 3 years for mature centres; own centres go from about INR 1 to 1.5 lakh in year 1 to above INR 3 lakh by year 3.
demand_pricing: Patient volume growth of 9.3% in Q4 organic and 7.5% for FY26; test volume growth of 8% for FY26 (organic).
Realisation improved about 5% in Q4 with no price hike taken that quarter.
Tier 3 and above growing 26% to 30% in recent quarters; Tier 1 growing about 11%; Mumbai growing 13% to 14%.
Insurance volumes are very small; portfolio still being built.
Management sees no third-party data on unorganised-to-organised shift, but says consumers and doctors are moving to larger brands.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give colour on mid-teens growth guidance, and any shift from unorganised players or online competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no third-party data but sees a shift to bigger brands; the 14% to 15% CAGR combines volume, RPP and some price increase. Specialty growth in oncology and neurology is seen as a tailwind.

qa_highlights.question: Will you take a price hike this fiscal, and what margin improvement is achievable next year?
qa_highlights.answer: No price increase planned now, but one may be taken later if needed. Management expects about 125 to 150 bps of EBITDA margin improvement in the coming year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 14% to 15% growth comes from volume versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8% to 9% from patient volume growth in the coming fiscal, with the remaining about 5% from realisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 20% productivity uplift for centres based on, and how does mini hub capex compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Same-centre productivity to rise 8% to 10% a year over 3 years. Mini hubs will cost about INR 30 to 40 lakh, higher than a collection centre and similar to a satellite lab.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the implied margin for the acquired businesses look low versus the stated high-single-digit Core margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intersegment revenue and margin eliminations between MHL and Core/Specialty explain the gap, with the benefit sitting in organic margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will intersegment eliminations persist, and should they be split between organic and inorganic EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Eliminations will persist as Core products are sold through the MHL network. From Q1 FY27 only one organic or company-level number will be reported.

risks_watch: Intersegment eliminations between MHL and Core/Specialty make the acquired-business margin hard to reconcile; watch how the organic and inorganic split is presented from Q1 FY27.
Depreciation rose sharply QoQ in Q4 (genomics machines, late-year capex, aggressive second-half network expansion), which could weigh on PAT.
Realisation growth depends on price increases that are not planned now; FY27 relies on about 5% realisation growth.
Margin path depends on lab platform upgrades and vendor consolidation, with benefits expected to strengthen over the next 2 quarters.
Inorganic growth depends on finding quality assets at the right price; management says many targets do not meet standards.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 delivery and the 3-year targets, with specific numbers given. Cautious on pricing (no hike now) and on M&A, which it will pursue only at the right price. Some answers on micro-market splits and lab utilisation were deliberately vague.
key_quotes: So, we'll definitely be looking at about 125 to 150 bps improvement in the coming year.

Anyone can add machines, but the real difference in results lies in the personalized interpretation needed for every patient, which rests on institutional expertise and knowledge, not on the equipment.
So, maximizing the EBITDA may not, in our mind, be a smarter strategy.
